name: underwater-ripple
title: Underwater Ripple
description: A scene seen from under moving water: three crossing wave fields refract the picture and split its colour a little at every ripple. The ripple closes on a whole number of cycles across the block, so it loops cleanly. Runs its WebGL shader over its own built-in scene (a stat and a bar chart; label, number and bars from variables), not over the host video.
useWhen: A scene should sit under water for its whole run: calm premium backdrops, ambient hero loops, a title card that needs motion without a direction.
The section loops, since the ripple closes exactly on a whole number of cycles.
avoidWhen: The water should be its own layer rather than something the scene is seen through: use shader-caustics behind a crisp scene.
The scene carries small type that has to stay legible: refraction bends every edge it touches.
You want a single travelling wave: nothing here sweeps.
author: Remocn

variables.label: Label
variables.description: Small caption above the number in the sample scene.

variables.label: Value
variables.description: The big number in the sample scene.

variables.label: Bars
variables.description: Bar heights as percentages, separated by commas (up to 12); the last bar is highlighted.

variables.label: Amplitude
variables.description: How far the picture is pushed by the ripples. Pixel sizes are for a 1280×720 frame and scale with the frame.

variables.label: Scale
variables.description: Size of the ripples; higher is finer.

variables.label: Speed
variables.description: Whole ripple cycles over the length of the block.

variables.label: Resolution
variables.description: Share of the frame size the shader is drawn at, then scaled up. Refraction is smooth; 0.75 matches 1 in the stills.
